text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parliament continues debate on 1997 fiscal budget and chamber expected to vote on the draft budget on Saturday.
- Release of eight people under a special royal pardon.
- Final draft of the customs law is completed and to be submitted to the cabinet soon before sending it to parliament for discussion and approval, customs department says.
- Information Minister hopes for an accord over an Israeli troop withdrawal from the West bank town of Hebron.
- Arab League head to visit Jordan early January to hold talk on Middle East peace process developments.
- Labour Minister says the U.N. may speed up compensation payments for victims of the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait.
- A large parliamentary vote expected in favour of the budget on Saturday.
- Pakistan ambassador to Jordan says his country preparing an economic accord with Jordan and is promoting joint ventures.
- King Hussein, Egyptian President Mubarak and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu likely to visit Washington early in 1997, U.S. officials say but no date fixed.
